note: Sections 10/11/12: Q8_0 VRAM accounting, SmolLM2-135M (30 layers) contexts 2048/8192/16384, and SmolLM2-360M (32 layers) ctx=2048. Weights ALWAYS full-GPU (mp.n_gpu_layers=-1) in every row below -- ONLY KV placement varies. Real external nvidia-smi measurement, same polling method used throughout this project. Raw data: raw_context_matrix_135m.jsonl, raw_q8_vram_16384.jsonl, raw_second_model_360m.jsonl.
critical_difference_from_phase12a: unlike Phase 12A's --gpu-layers N (which moved weights AND KV together), every row here keeps ALL weight layers GPU-resident (verified per placement_maps.json) -- the VRAM delta below is caused by KV placement ALONE, the isolated effect Phase 12A could not achieve.

findings.saving_grows_with_context: 12 -> 48 -> 96 MiB (half-split) as ctx grows 2048 -> 8192 -> 16384 on 135M, consistent with the saving being proportional to per-layer KV bytes, which scale with context length -- exactly what a KV-specific (not weight-specific) mechanism should look like
findings.saving_is_modest_at_small_context: at ctx=2048, KV is a small fraction of total footprint (weights dominate) for both models, so absolute savings are correspondingly small (12-21 MiB) -- not a weakness of the mechanism, just an expected consequence of KV being a small share of memory at low context
findings.second_model_confirms_generality: the pattern (real, monotonic, weights-unaffected VRAM reduction) reproduces on a different layer count (32 vs 30) and different per-layer KV width without any code change
